sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
My 3x3 extraction was wrong — I was outputting the wrong rows. Let me redo it: eye(22,28) returns 36 characters (6x6). I output e1[i*2] for i in range(3) — this is the even-indexed characters of the first row only, not a 3x3. My mistake: e1 is a flat list of 36 characters (row-major, 6 per row). e1[i*2] for i in 0..2 = characters 0, 2, 4 = the even columns of the first row. So "eye1 3x3: ['W','g','g'] ['W','g','g']" was wrong — both lists were actually from row 0 and… no wait, I output two lists: [e1[i*2] for i in range(3)] and [e1[i*2+1] for i in range(3)] — both from row 0! The segs() function was using e[i*2+j] with i,j in 0..2 — this is also wrong: it was only reading row 0 (indices 0-5) and treating it as 3x3.
I need to redo this properly: the 3x3 at 2x2 block positions is e[i*6 + j*2] (i,j in 0..2).
Let me recompute.

a = current_frame.ascii.split('\n')
def eye3(r0,c0):
    return [[a[r0+i*2][c0+j*2] for j in range(3)] for i in range(3)]
e1 = eye3(22,28); e2 = eye3(38,28)
print("eye1:", e1); print("eye2:", e2)
segmap = {(0,1):'N',(1,0):'W',(1,2):'E',(2,1):'S',(0,0):'NW',(0,2):'NE',(2,0):'SW',(2,2):'SE'}
def segs(e):
    return [nm for (i,j),nm in segmap.items() if e[i][j]=='W']
s1, s2 = segs(e1), segs(e2)
print("eye1 segs:", s1, "eye2 segs:", s2)
cells = {(0,0):(16,22),(0,1):(16,30),(0,2):(16,38),
         (1,0):(24,22),(1,2):(24,38),
         (2,0):(32,22),(2,1):(32,30),(2,2):(32,38),
         (3,0):(40,22),(3,2):(40,38),
         (4,0):(48,22),(4,1):(48,30),(4,2):(48,38)}
D = {'N':(-1,0),'S':(1,0),'W':(0,-1),'E':(0,1),'NW':(-1,-1),'NE':(-1,1),'SW':(1,-1),'SE':(1,1)}
want = set()
for nm in s1: want.add((1+D[nm][0], 1+D[nm][1]))
for nm in s2: want.add((3+D[nm][0], 1+D[nm][1]))
print("target cells:", sorted(want))
print("clicks:", [cells[k] for k in sorted(want)])
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
